cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at Heapify up method, which is going to be used inside the insert
method.
So this is our binary heap.
And we have inserted 100 over here.
Now we know that this is max binary heap.
That's why the main property of the binary heap is violated.
Because 100 has to be the root node in this case.
Now for this after insertion we are doing heapify up.
So we are going to declare the heapify up method like this, which is going to take as a parameter index.
Now the index is going to be the node's index that we have inserted.
So we have inserted 100 which means that the index is going to be seven in this case.
Then the next thing that we are going to do we are going to create a variable over here, which is going
to be current index.
And initially we are going to assign the value of the parameter to this current index.
In this case it is seven, which means that current index is going to be seven.
Then based on the current index, we are going to find out the parent index of the current index.
So in this case the current index is seven.
And in seven we have 100.
And the parent of 100 is 60.
And 60 is located at the index of three, which means that the parent index is going to be three.
Then we are going to write the loop like this.
So while the current index is greater than zero, we see that it is seven, which means that it is greater
than zero.
And we are going to compare the current index with the parent index.
If this condition is true, we see that in this case the current index is seven and the parent index
is three.
So the value in the current index which is 100 is greater than 60.
So this compare method is going to return true.
So this means that this while loop will be executed.
Then inside the while loop we are going to call the swap method that we have declared before.
So the swap method will swap values of the cells which are located in the current index, and the parent
index.
Now, in the current index we have 100, and in the parent index we have 60.
So this means that their places will be swapped.
Now 100 is located at the index of three and 60 is located at the index of seven.
Then we are going to update the current index.
Now currently the current index is going to be the parent index.
Now the parent index is three.
So this means that the current index will become three.
Then we are going to update the parent index as well based on the current index.
Now the current index is three which is 100.
Now the parent of 100 is 80 which is located at the index of one.
So this means that the parent index is going to be one.
Then one more time the execution will come to the loop and check that if the current index is greater
than zero, we see that it is three and it is greater.
The value in the current index, which is 100, is greater than the value that is located at the index
of one, which is 80.
That's why this condition will return true.
And we are going to go ahead and swap these values.
Now after swapping them one more time, we need to calculate the current index.
So this means that the parent index will become the current index which is one, and the based on the
one which is current index.
We are going to find out the parent index.
Now at the index of one we have 100 and the parent of 100 is 90.
So this means that the parent index will become zero because 90 is located at the index of zero.
Then one more time loop will come over here.
Current index is greater than zero.
And if we compare the values in the current index and the parent index, we see that in the current
index the value is greater than the parent index.
That's why we're just going to go ahead and swap them.
So after swapping them 100 will become the root of this binary heap.
So as you can see the property is maintained.
So here again we are going to calculate the current index which is going to be in this case zero.
And the parent index also is going to be zero.
Because the current index is zero and it does not have any parent.
That's why it's going to return zero.
So after doing so the current index is zero.
So this means that the execution of while loop will be stopped.
So the method will stop over here because the main property of binary heap is maintained.
Now we are going to go ahead and take this method and put it inside the insert method that we have declared
before.
So this is the insert method we have called over here push method of the array.
Then we have put over here dot dot for heapify up.
That's why here all we have to do is we're just going to bring the heapify up with the last index.
Now, to be able to access the last index, we are going to access the Len of this array.
In this case we have eight elements in this array.
So if we put minus one it's going to be the seven.
So at the index of seven we have inserted 100.
So heapify up method should be called on this element to maintain the main property of the binary heap.
So that's how the Heapify up method looks like.
Now in the next lecture, let's put everything together inside the binary heap class and find out time
and space complexity for each method separately.
